chunks: And by the first chain, he said:

And regarding the chest, when it is bruised so both of its sides are bent, its wergild is five hundred Dinars; and the wergild of one side when it is bent is two hundred and fifty Dinars; and when the chest and the two shoulders are bent, its wergild is one thousand Dinars; and if one of the sides of the chest and one of the shoulders are bent, its wergild is five hundred Dinars; and the wergild of the exposure of the chest is twenty-five Dinars; and the wergild of the exposure of the shoulders and the back is twenty-five Dinars; and if the man gets twisted from that, not being able to turn around, its wergild is five hundred Dinars. So if the spine breaks, and it is bandaged and there is no flaw, its wergild is one hundred Dinars; and if there remains a flaw, its wergild is one thousand Dinars; and regarding the nipple of the breast of the man, the wergild is one hundred and twenty-five Dinars.
ai.seo_question: What is the diyah (blood money) for a broken chest or spine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elaborates on the jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money) for male-specific injuries, detailing precise compensations for trauma to the chest, shoulders, and spine based on the degree of impairment and residual defect (*'ithm*). It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing between temporary disability and permanent deformity, ensuring equitable restitution for bodily integrity as derived from the Imams' teachings.

en.hubeali: And by the first chain, he<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘And regarding the chest when it is bruised, so both of its sides are bent, its wergild is five hundred Dinars; and wergild of one side when it is bent, is two hundred and fifty Dinars; and when the chest and the two shoulders are bent, its wergild is one thousand Dinars; and if one of the side of the chest is bent and one of the shoulders, so its wergild is five hundred Dinars; and wergild of the exposure of the chest is twenty-five Dinars; and wergild of the exposure of the shoulder and the back is twenty five Dinars; and if the man gets twisted from that, not being able to turn around, so its wergild is five hundred Dinars. So if the spine breaks, and it is bandaged upon and there is no fault, so its wergild is one hundred Dinars; and if there remains a flaw, so its wergild is one thousand Dinars; and regarding the nipple of the breast of the man is damaged, the wergild is one hundred and twenty five Dinars’.
